18	// section is one titled box of the dashboard. Sections are declared in a
19	// table rather than as that many render*Section methods: that's what makes
20	// the rule "a section declares its height and fills it" checkable for all
21	// of them at once (§3.19 phase 1).
22	type section struct {
23		title string
24		// render returns the box's content lines. It returns the *same count* of
25		// them whatever the state of the data — that's the contract
26		// TestEverySectionKeepsItsHeightWhateverItsState checks.
27		render func(m Model, width int, t tier) []string
28	}
29	
30	// labelWidth aligns every label column of every box on one width.
31	const labelWidth = 11
32	
33	// overviewSections returns the four boxes of the Overview tab, in reading
34	// order: the two text boxes first, then the two that carry a chart.
35	//
36	// The grouping is by question asked, not by data source — hence two
37	// merges: workspaces joins GitLab (the explorer creates, workspaces
38	// reconciles: one subject seen from both ends) and the tools join Host
39	// (they are this machine's binaries, measured by the same probe).
40	func overviewSections(forgeType string) []section {
41		return []section{
42			{title: theme.ForgeIcon(forgeType) + " Code", render: renderCodeSection},
43			{title: theme.IconSecurity + " Health", render: renderHealthSection},
44			{title: theme.IconServer + " " + hostLabel(), render: renderHostSection},
45			{title: engineSectionTitle(), render: renderDockerSection},
46		}
47	}
48	
49	// resourceSections returns the boxes of the Resources tab — inline in the
50	// third column at `wide`. They exist only because no view shows them: there
51	// is no :host, and :containers shows a container, not the machine.
52	func resourceSections() []section {
53		return []section{
54			{title: theme.IconArrowDown + " Network", render: renderNetworkSection},
55			{title: theme.IconDirectory + " Storage", render: renderStorageSection},
56		}
57	}

59	// hostLabel names the measurement point rather than the machine. gopsutil reads
60	// the OS dk runs on, while docker stats reads inside the Docker Desktop VM:
61	// both are true and they do not add up.
62	func hostLabel() string {
63		switch runtime.GOOS {
64		case "windows":
65			return "Host (Windows)"
66		case "darwin":
67			return "Host (macOS)"
68		default:
69			return "Host (Linux)"
70		}
71	}

73	func renderCodeSection(m Model, width int, t tier) []string {
74		v := m.vocab()
75		// The icon follows the value: the value column then starts at the same
76		// place on every line, which an icon up front would shift by one cell
77		// only on the lines that carry one.
78		sessionLine := theme.DimStyle.Render("not connected") + theme.Bg("  ") + theme.DimStyle.Render(theme.IconError)
79		if m.shared.IsAuthenticated {
80			sessionLine = theme.PrimaryColorStyle.Bold(true).Render(m.shared.CurrentUser.Username) +
81				theme.Bg("  ") + theme.StatusOKStyle.Render(theme.IconOK)
82		}
83	
84		mrs, review, issues := unknownValue(), unknownValue(), unknownValue()
85		if m.forgeStats != nil {
86			mrs = maybeCountValue(m.forgeStats.AssignedChangeRequests)
87			review = maybeCountValue(m.forgeStats.ReviewChangeRequests)
88			issues = maybeCountValue(m.forgeStats.AssignedIssues)
89		}
90	
91		workspaces := unknownValue()
92		if !m.loadingWorkspaces {
93			workspaces = countValue(m.workspaceCount)
94		}
95	
96		if t != tierWide {
97			return []string{
98				sessionLine,
99				row(v.ChangeRequestShort+"s", mrs+theme.Bg(" assigned  ")+review+theme.Bg(" to review")),
100				row("Issues", issues+theme.Bg(" assigned")),
101				theme.Bg(""),
102				row("Workspaces", workspaces),
103				theme.DimStyle.Render(truncatePath(m.config.App.WorkspacesDir, width-labelWidth)),
104			}
105		}
106	
107		// At `wide`, the box becomes two trees, and the split is §3.16's two
108		// halves: the explorer creates what doesn't exist — the forge — and
109		// workspaces reconciles what does — the disk. Each has its own question,
110		// so each has its own root, and the forge's facts stop floating above a
111		// tree they don't belong to.
112		//
113		// The counters become branches there: "0 assigned  0 to review" on one
114		// line requires rereading the sentence to know which is which, two
115		// nodes say it by lining them up.
116		// The qualifier is in the label, not in the value: "issues 0 assigned"
117		// and "MR assigned  0" said the same thing two different ways, and the
118		// value column then didn't carry the same kind of thing everywhere. The
119		// three counters now read in a column.
120		pathWidth := theme.BoxContentWidth(width) - treeValueColumn
121		return []string{
122			theme.Bg(v.Name),
123			branch(false, "user", sessionLine),
124			branch(false, "host", theme.Bg(forgeHost(m.config.Forge.URL))),
125			branch(false, "issues assigned", issues),
126			branch(false, v.ChangeRequestShort+" assigned", mrs),
127			branch(true, v.ChangeRequestShort+" to review", review),
128			treeGap(),
129			theme.Bg("Workspaces"),
130			branch(false, "repositories", workspaces),
131			branch(false, "path", theme.DimStyle.Render(truncatePath(m.config.App.WorkspacesDir, pathWidth))),
132			branch(true, "disk", treeSize(m.wsSize)),
133		}
134	}

136	// treeGap separates two trees stacked in one box. The last node's elbow
137	// says where one tree ends, but not that another begins: without this
138	// line, the two roots read as two more nodes.
139	func treeGap() string { return theme.Bg("") }
140	
141	// treeSize renders what the workspaces occupy.
142	//
143	// **This is the tree's size, not the volume's fill level.** What these
144	// repositories cost is what you can act on — deleting one frees the space —
145	// whereas the volume mixes the workspaces in with the rest of the machine.
146	// The Host box keeps the free space, which is the other question.
147	//
148	// It comes at a cost: it's the only dashboard figure whose measurement
149	// walks the entire tree. See metrics.Size and Model.measuringSize.
150	func treeSize(size metrics.TreeSize) string {
151		if !size.OK {
152			return unknownValue()
153		}
154		out := theme.Bg(humanBytes(size.Bytes))
155		if size.Partial {
156			// A directory that denies access makes the total an underestimate,
157			// and an underestimated total with no mention reads as a
158			// measurement.
159			out += theme.DimStyle.Render("  partial")
160		}
161		return out
162	}
163	
164	// forgeHost strips the scheme off the configured forge URL: it's the host
165	// that identifies the instance, and `https://` is true of all of them.
166	func forgeHost(rawURL string) string {
167		host := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(rawURL, "https://"), "http://")
168		return strings.TrimSuffix(host, "/")
169	}
170	
171	// treeLabelWidth aligns the values of a tree's nodes, indent included. It
172	// is sized on the application's longest label — `issues assigned`, fifteen
173	// cells — because a label that overflows doesn't just break the alignment
174	// of its own line: it opens a second value column in the box.
175	// TestEveryTreeNodeAlignsItsValue checks it against every section.
176	const treeLabelWidth = 17
177	
178	// treeStemWidth is what IconTreeBranch and IconTreeEnd occupy: two
179	// box-drawing characters and the space after them. It is written rather
180	// than measured because a constant cannot call lipgloss.Width, and
181	// TestATreeRowLinesUpWithItsBranches checks it against the actual
182	// rendering.
183	const treeStemWidth = 3
184	
185	// treeValueColumn is where a tree node's value begins.
186	const treeValueColumn = treeStemWidth + treeLabelWidth - 1
187	
188	// narrowTreeLabelWidth is the same column inside a **split** box, where each
189	// tree gets half the width.
190	//
191	// It is sized on `reclaimable`, eleven cells, the longest label of the
192	// three boxes concerned. The wide column would cost three more value cells
193	// there, out of the eleven a half-box leaves at the narrowest `wide` tier
194	// (180 columns) — enough to truncate `3 days ago`.
195	const (
196		narrowTreeLabelWidth  = 14
197		narrowTreeValueColumn = treeStemWidth + narrowTreeLabelWidth - 1
198	)
199	
200	// branch renders one node of a tree. `last` picks the corner, so the run of
201	// nodes has a visible end — without it, two trees in a row read as one.
202	func branch(last bool, label, value string) string {
203		return branchAt(treeLabelWidth, last, label, value)
204	}
205	
206	// narrowBranch is a node of a tree that shares its box with another, side by
207	// side.
208	func narrowBranch(last bool, label, value string) string {
209		return branchAt(narrowTreeLabelWidth, last, label, value)
210	}
211	
212	func branchAt(column int, last bool, label, value string) string {
213		stem := theme.IconTreeBranch
214		if last {
215			stem = theme.IconTreeEnd
216		}
217		padded := label
218		if n := column - len(label) - 2; n > 0 {
219			padded = label + strings.Repeat(" ", n)
220		}
221		return theme.DimStyle.Render(stem) + theme.Bg(padded+" ") + value
222	}
223	
224	// sideBySide lays two runs of lines out as two columns of one box.
225	//
226	// The cut is in the middle, and each half is **truncated** rather than let
227	// to overflow: a line too long on the left would shift the whole right
228	// column, and a line too long on the right would overflow the box, which
229	// RenderTitledBox would cut anyway — but after breaking the alignment (Rule
230	// 116).
231	//
232	// The assembly is done line by line with PadWithBg and never with
233	// lipgloss.JoinHorizontal, which inserts bare spaces that let the
234	// terminal's native background show through (Rule 115).
235	func sideBySide(left, right []string, width int) []string {
236		half := max(width/2, 1)
237		out := make([]string, max(len(left), len(right)))
238		for i := range out {
239			var l, r string
240			if i < len(left) {
241				// The gutter is subtracted from the left column, not added to the
242				// right: without it, a value that fills its half touches the
243				// elbow of the first node next to it and the two read as one.
244				l = theme.Truncate(left[i], half-columnGutter)
245			}
246			if i < len(right) {
247				r = theme.Truncate(right[i], width-half)
248			}
249			out[i] = theme.PadWithBg(l, half) + r
250		}
251		return out
252	}
253	
254	// columnGutter is the blank kept between two columns of one box.
255	const columnGutter = 2
256	
257	// padRuns lengthens a run with blank lines. The padding is **empty of
258	// content**, not padded to width: sideBySide lays down the whole line's
259	// background (Rule 115).
260	func padRuns(run []string, height int) []string {
261		out := make([]string, 0, max(height, len(run)))
262		out = append(out, run...)
263		for len(out) < height {
264			out = append(out, theme.Bg(""))
265		}
266		return out
267	}
268	
269	func renderHealthSection(m Model, width int, t tier) []string {
270		if t == tierWide {
271			left, right := healthColumns(m)
272			return sideBySide(left, right, theme.BoxContentWidth(width))
273		}
274	
275		monitors, certs := unknownValue(), unknownValue()
276		if !m.loadingServices {
277			monitors = statusSummary(m.filterComponents(false))
278			certs = certSummary(m.filterComponents(true))
279		}
280		expiry := nearestExpiry(m.filterComponents(true), m.loadingServices, true)
281	
282		// Six lines, not seven: the blank line that used to separate monitoring
283		// from security paid for the certificate expiry. A seventh line here
284		// would overflow the whole overview.
285		total := m.posture.Total()
286		scanned, critical, oldest := unknownValue(), unknownValue(), unknownValue()
287		if m.posture.Read {
288			scanned = countValue(total.Targets) + theme.Bg(" targets")
289			critical = severityCount(total.Critical) + theme.Bg("  ") +
290				unscannedValue(m.unscannedTotal()) + theme.DimStyle.Render(" unscanned")
291			oldest = scanAge(total)
292		}
293	
294		return []string{
295			row("Monitors", monitors),
296			row("Certs", certs),
297			row("Expiry", expiry),
298			row("Scanned", scanned),
299			row("Critical", critical),
300			row("Oldest", oldest),
301		}
302	}
303	
304	// healthColumns splits the box in two, and the split is by **subject rather
305	// than by kind**: supervision on the left with the repositories it watches over,
306	// certificates on the right with the images. The four trees used to fit in one
307	// column at nineteen lines, which made Health the tallest box in its row and
308	// cropped the other three boxes' curves by that much.
309	//
310	// They are rendered separately from their assembly: that's what lets them
311	// be checked one by one, since once joined the nodes of both trees share a
312	// line.
313	func healthColumns(m Model) (left, right []string) {
314		unscannedImages, imagesMeasured := m.unscannedImages()
315		unscannedRepos, reposMeasured := m.unscannedRepositories()
316	
317		monitors := append([]string{theme.Bg("Monitors")},
318			statusBranches(m.filterComponents(false), m.loadingServices)...)
319	
320		// The expiry hangs from Certs rather than floating above: it's a fact
321		// about the certificates, and it only makes sense there. The
322		// certificate's name dropped along with the split into two columns —
323		// the half-width box doesn't hold it — and it's :status that owns the
324		// named list.
325		//
326		// This extra node is also what shifts the two columns: without the
327		// catch-up below, `Repositories` would start a line above `Images` and
328		// the two bottom trees would read like a staircase.
329		certs := m.filterComponents(true)
330		certTree := append([]string{theme.Bg("Certs")},
331			certBranches(certs, m.loadingServices, nearestExpiry(certs, m.loadingServices, false))...)
332	
333		top := max(len(monitors), len(certTree))
334		left = append(padRuns(monitors, top), treeGap(), theme.Bg("Repositories"))
335		left = append(left, postureBranches(m.posture, m.posture.Repositories, unscannedRepos, reposMeasured)...)
336	
337		right = append(padRuns(certTree, top), treeGap(), theme.Bg("Images"))
338		right = append(right, postureBranches(m.posture, m.posture.Images, unscannedImages, imagesMeasured)...)
339	
340		return left, right
341	}
342	
343	// statusBranches renders one node per monitor state. All three states are
344	// always there, including at zero: a missing branch reads as a state that
345	// isn't monitored, which is the opposite of what a zero means.
346	//
347	// Certificates no longer go through here — see certBranches, and
348	// status.CertState for what tells them apart.
349	func statusBranches(components []status.ComponentStatus, loading bool) []string {
350		nodes := func(up, down, errValue string) []string {
351			return []string{
352				narrowBranch(false, "up", up),
353				narrowBranch(false, "down", down),
354				narrowBranch(true, "error", errValue),
355			}
356		}
357	
358		switch {
359		case loading:
360			return nodes(unknownValue(), unknownValue(), unknownValue())
361		case len(components) == 0:
362			return nothingConfigured(len(nodes("", "", "")))
363		default:
364			ok, down, errCount := countStatuses(components)
365			return nodes(
366				countValue(ok)+theme.Bg("  ")+theme.StatusOKStyle.Render(theme.IconOK),
367				alertCount(down, theme.IconError, theme.StatusDownStyle),
368				alertCount(errCount, theme.IconWarning, theme.StatusErrorStyle),
369			)
370		}
371	}
372	
373	// certBranches renders one node per certificate state, then the nearest
374	// expiry.
375	//
376	// **The vocabulary is not the monitors', and that was the bug.** A
377	// certificate rendered under `up` / `down` / `error` put an expired
378	// certificate, one expiring next week, and one that couldn't be read —
379	// SSLChecker gives `ERROR` to all three — into the same bucket, while `up`
380	// named "reachable" which means "valid". The four states of
381	// status.CertState tell them apart, and the one line that calls for action —
382	// `to renew` — stops being drowned in the other two.
383	//
384	// The expiry stays its own node: `to renew` says how many, it says when,
385	// and two figures on one line require remembering which is which (that's
386	// what postureBranches already settled).
387	func certBranches(certs []status.ComponentStatus, loading bool, expiry string) []string {
388		nodes := func(valid, toRenew, expired, errValue string) []string {
389			return []string{
390				narrowBranch(false, "valid", valid),
391				narrowBranch(false, "to renew", toRenew),
392				narrowBranch(false, "expired", expired),
393				narrowBranch(false, "error", errValue),
394				narrowBranch(true, "expiry", expiry),
395			}
396		}
397	
398		switch {
399		case loading:
400			return nodes(unknownValue(), unknownValue(), unknownValue(), unknownValue())
401		case len(certs) == 0:
402			return nothingConfigured(len(nodes("", "", "", "")))
403		default:
404			valid, toRenew, expired, errored := status.CertCounts(certs)
405			return nodes(
406				countValue(valid)+theme.Bg("  ")+certGlyph(status.CertValid),
407				certAlert(toRenew, status.CertToRenew),
408				certAlert(expired, status.CertExpired),
409				certAlert(errored, status.CertError),
410			)
411		}
412	}
413	
414	// certGlyph and certAlert read one state's glyph and colour from the theme
415	// rather than naming them here: `:status` renders the same column, and two
416	// lookup tables would eventually diverge on the one that matters — the one
417	// that tells `expired` apart from `error`.
418	func certGlyph(state status.CertState) string {
419		return theme.CertStateStyle(string(state)).Render(theme.CertStateIcon(string(state)))
420	}
421	
422	func certAlert(n int, state status.CertState) string {
423		return alertCount(n, theme.CertStateIcon(string(state)), theme.CertStateStyle(string(state)))
424	}
425	
426	// nothingConfigured says a tree watches nothing, and keeps the height it
427	// would have had — a box that shrinks shifts its entire row.
428	func nothingConfigured(height int) []string {
429		out := []string{narrowBranch(true, "configured", theme.DimStyle.Render("none"))}
430		for range height - 1 {
431			out = append(out, theme.Bg(""))
432		}
433		return out
434	}
435	
436	// alertCount renders one non-nominal state's tally. The glyph is the
437	// state's own — a cross for DOWN, an alert for ERROR, an hourglass for a
438	// coming renewal, :status's vocabulary — including at zero: a check mark on
439	// the "down" line said "everything is fine" right where one is looking for
440	// how many are down, and it's the line's state an icon names, not its
441	// count.
442	//
443	// It's the color that carries the count: dimmed at zero, because a red
444	// cross on "0 down" teaches the reader the color instead of alerting them.
445	// The icon stays to the right of the number, as everywhere else.
446	//
447	// The number and the icon share **the same** style — the caller's, not a
448	// fixed red: a certificate `to renew` is a warning (orange), not a finding
449	// (severityCount's red), and a number colored one way next to an icon
450	// colored another says the same fact twice in two different colors.
451	func alertCount(n int, glyph string, style lipgloss.Style) string {
452		if n == 0 {
453			return countValue(0) + theme.Bg("  ") + theme.DimStyle.Render(glyph)
454		}
455		return style.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d", n)) + theme.Bg("  ") + style.Render(glyph)
456	}
457	
458	// postureBranches renders one family's tally, one figure per node.
459	//
460	// Each figure gets its own branch rather than sharing a line: two numbers
461	// side by side require remembering which is which, and that's exactly the
462	// figure read in a hurry.
463	//
464	// `unscanned` took HIGH's place because it's actionable: it names the
465	// targets the whole box says nothing about, and the answer is to run a
466	// scan. One more HIGH changed no decision the CRITICAL above hadn't already
467	// made.
468	func postureBranches(p posture, side postureSide, unscanned int, measured bool) []string {
469		if !p.Read {
470			return []string{
471				narrowBranch(false, "scanned", unknownValue()),
472				narrowBranch(false, "critical", unknownValue()),
473				narrowBranch(false, "secrets", unknownValue()),
474				narrowBranch(false, "unscanned", unknownValue()),
475				narrowBranch(true, "oldest", unknownValue()),
476			}
477		}
478		return []string{
479			narrowBranch(false, "scanned", countValue(side.Targets)+theme.Bg(" targets")),
480			narrowBranch(false, "critical", severityCount(side.Critical)),
481			narrowBranch(false, "secrets", secretsValue(side)),
482			narrowBranch(false, "unscanned", unscannedValue(unscanned, measured)),
483			narrowBranch(true, "oldest", scanAge(side)),
484		}
485	}
486	
487	// secretsValue renders how many targets carry a secret.
488	//
489	// These are targets and not secrets: two repositories are two decisions,
490	// forty leaks in the same one are only one, and it's the inventory (:sec)
491	// that breaks it down.
492	//
493	// `-` when no verdict at all is known, which is not a theoretical
494	// precaution: `scan.enable_secret` turned off, a missing tool, or entries
495	// written before the image scan had a secrets step — in all three cases a
496	// `0` would say "no target carries any" for targets nobody has looked at. A
497	// verdict known on only part of the set is enough to display the count: it's
498	// then a floor, and a nonzero floor is actionable.
499	func secretsValue(side postureSide) string {
500		if side.SecretsKnown == 0 {
501			return unknownValue()
502		}
503		return severityCount(side.Secrets)
504	}
505	
506	// unscannedValue renders a coverage gap. It does not take severityCount's
507	// red: a never-scanned target has no CRITICAL, it has an unknown, and the
508	// two are not fixed the same way. Nor does it take countValue's purple — a
509	// gap in coverage is an attention signal like `to renew`, not a neutral
510	// tally like `scanned`: warnCount keeps purple reserved for facts that
511	// carry no risk of their own.
512	func unscannedValue(n int, measured bool) string {
513		if !measured {
514			return unknownValue()
515		}
516		return warnCount(n)
517	}
518	
519	// severityCount colours a finding count only when there is one to find. A
520	// zero in red teaches the reader the color instead of alerting them.
521	func severityCount(n int) string {
522		if n == 0 {
523			return theme.DimStyle.Render("0")
524		}
525		return theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d", n))
526	}
527	
528	// warnCount is severityCount's orange counterpart, for a number that
529	// deserves attention but is not itself a security finding — a coverage gap,
530	// something approaching rather than something wrong.
531	func warnCount(n int) string {
532		if n == 0 {
533			return theme.DimStyle.Render("0")
534		}
535		return theme.StatusWarningStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d", n))
536	}
537	
538	// scanAge renders how stale the oldest scan is. A CRITICAL count three
539	// weeks old is counting code that no longer exists.
540	// `never` rather than "nothing scanned": under a node called `oldest` the
541	// long sentence repeats the label, and a half-width box at the narrowest
542	// `wide` tier only holds eleven value cells.
543	func scanAge(side postureSide) string {
544		if side.Targets == 0 {
545			return theme.DimStyle.Render("never")
546		}
547		if side.Oldest.IsZero() {
548			return unknownValue()
549		}

553	// nearestExpiry renders the deadline that comes first — the only one of
554	// the N dates that calls for a decision.
555	//
556	// **It only looks at what is still running.** A certificate already expired
557	// has no countdown left, and rendering it as "-2 days" required the reader
558	// to translate a negative number into a fact the `expired` node already
559	// states. Nothing ahead, then, reads `-`: that's what the line has always
560	// meant when it has no date to give.
561	//
562	// `named` is false in a shared column: a half-width box does not hold "58
563	// days  registry.example.com", and it's the number of days that's
564	// actionable. The named list belongs to :status, which already owns it.
565	func nearestExpiry(certs []status.ComponentStatus, loading, named bool) string {
566		if loading {
567			return unknownValue()
568		}
569		if len(certs) == 0 {
570			return theme.DimStyle.Render("none configured")
571		}
572	
573		var soonest *status.ComponentStatus
574		for i, c := range certs {
575			switch status.CertStateOf(c) {
576			case status.CertValid, status.CertToRenew:
577			default:
578				// Expired or unreadable: both have their node, and neither has an
579				// expiry still ahead.
580				continue
581			}
582			if soonest == nil || *c.SSLDaysLeft < *soonest.SSLDaysLeft {
583				soonest = &certs[i]
584			}
585		}
586		if soonest == nil {
587			return unknownValue()
588		}
589	
590		// The threshold is exactly CertStateOf's "to renew" one — soonest is
591		// never CertExpired here (excluded above) — so this is warning-orange,
592		// the same color the `to renew` node already renders it in: an expiry
593		// close enough to act on is not yet the red of an actual failure.
594		days := *soonest.SSLDaysLeft
595		value := theme.Bg(fmt.Sprintf("%d days", days))
596		if days <= status.CertRenewWindowDays {
597			value = theme.StatusWarningStyle.Render(fmt.Sprintf("%d days", days))
598		}
599		if !named {
600			return value
601		}
602		return value + theme.DimStyle.Render("  "+soonest.Name)
603	}

884		// In both cases there is no throughput — `-`, not `0`.
885		rx, tx := unknownValue(), unknownValue()

887		if m.host.HasRate {
888			// The cumulative total rides on the same line as the rate it is the
889			// integral of (§3.69): "1.2 MB/s · 340 MB". It is folded into the
890			// same condition as the rate rather than shown on its own — on the
891			// very first tick the total is trivially zero, and showing it a
892			// beat later, once there is also a rate to put it beside, says more.
893			rx = theme.Bg(humanBytes(uint64(m.host.NetRXPerSec))) + theme.DimStyle.Render("/s")
894			tx = theme.Bg(humanBytes(uint64(m.host.NetTXPerSec))) + theme.DimStyle.Render("/s")
895			if totals.Valid {
896				rx += netTotalSuffix(totals.RX)
897				tx += netTotalSuffix(totals.TX)
898			}
899		}

901		// Throughput has no known ceiling: the scale stays automatic, against a
902		// fixed 0-to-100 scale for a percentage.

908		// throughput is missing is kept in it anyway. What it might have said —
909		// that the window is not full yet — the curve already says on its own: a
910		// partial series is drawn right-aligned, so the blank on its left *is* the
911		// history it does not have.

915		lines = append(lines, chartOf(m, width, t, func(s metrics.HostSample) float64 { return s.NetTXPerSec }, 0)...)
